# Closing the Digital Evidence Gap in Violence Against Women and Girls Investigations


September 24, 2026


|[Cellebrite](https://cellebrite.com/en/author/admin/)


## **Key Takeaways**


- Digital evidence sits at the centre of most serious VAWG cases, but slow extraction holds prosecutions back.
- Device data can prove coercive control, place suspects at a scene and break false alibis.
- Faster device processing means fewer repeat victim interviews and fewer cases lost on evidential gaps.
- Cellebrite Inseyets covers extraction, encrypted apps, deleted data and court-ready reporting for VAWG cases.


**Every device holds a story. The question is whether investigators can access it in time.**


Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) is one of the most prevalent — and most consistently undercharged — categories of[serious crime across EMEA](https://cellebrite.com/en/organised-crime/) . Legislative reform has moved fast: the U.K.’s Domestic Abuse Act, Germany’s expanded stalking provisions and similar updates across the region. Conviction rates have not kept pace, and the gap between reported offenses and successful prosecution remains stubbornly wide.


At the heart of that gap is a digital evidence problem. The communications, location data, deleted messages, photographs and application histories that document coercion and abuse already exist. What’s missing, in many units, is the forensic capability to access them at the pace an active investigation demands.


## **The Scale of the Evidence Gap**


More than fifty million VAWG offenses are recorded across EMEA every year, and the majority leave a digital trail. Yet delayed or incomplete digital evidence extraction remains the number one barrier to prosecution.


- Seventy-eight percent of serious VAWG cases involve a digital device as the primary evidence source
- Agencies using digital forensics workflows report case closure up to 43% faster


When digital evidence is delayed, incomplete or ruled inadmissible, the cost extends well beyond any single case. Victims face repeat interviews, which can compound trauma. Perpetrators who remain active present an escalating risk. Cases collapse in court through evidentiary gaps, and investigators managing manual review at volume face real burnout.


## **How Digital Evidence Strengthens VAWG Cases**


Modern digital forensics, deployed correctly, does not just speed up an investigation — it changes what is provable. The shift is operational, legal and humanitarian, not merely technological.


**Coercive control** is difficult to prove through victim testimony alone. Patterns documented across months of communications data establish the sustained nature of abuse without requiring a victim to carry the case unsupported.


**Location intelligence** — GPS data, cell tower records, application location histories — places suspects at scenes, contradicts false alibis and documents harassment patterns over time.


**Encrypted applications** are no longer a dead end. Advanced extraction capabilities now access content from the platforms suspects use most, surfacing evidence that was previously invisible to investigators.


**Rapid triage,** powered by AI-assisted prioritization, surfaces the most evidentially significant content quickly, cutting the time between device recovery and actionable intelligence.


**Court-ready reporting** generates documentation that meets admissibility standards across EMEA jurisdictions, reducing the risk of a case being challenged on process rather than merit.


## **What Faster Evidence Means in Practice**


In one coercive control case handled by an EMEA law enforcement agency, investigators using Cellebrite INSEYETS recovered eighteen months of deleted WhatsApp messages within four hours of device recovery. The case proceeded to conviction without the victim having to give live evidence.


That outcome is consistent with what agencies across the region report after integrating Cellebrite’s capabilities into VAWG investigation workflows: faster processing, stronger evidence packages and measurably better outcomes for victims.


- Average digital evidence processing time down 40–60% across peer agencies
- Significant reduction in repeat victim interviews and associated trauma
- Higher guilty-plea rates where digital evidence is strong and complete
- Improved investigator confidence and reduced caseload pressure


*“We went from weeks to hours,” said one digital forensics lead at an EMEA law enforcement agency. “The impact on victim welfare and case success rates has been transformational.”*

## Digital Evidence in VAWG Cases: FAQ


**What digital forensics tools can be used in VAWG investigations?**


Cellebrite Inseyets, a digital forensics solution, is used in VAWG investigations to extract and analyse phone data, including messages, location history and app data. It works across major device types, recovers encrypted app content and deleted data, and produces court-ready reports.


**What digital evidence is useful in coercive control cases?**


The most useful evidence is messages, call logs, location history and app data that show monitoring, threats or restriction over weeks or months. Cellebrite Inseyets recovers this data, including deleted messages, and builds it into a timeline that shows the pattern of behaviour beyond the victim’s account.


**How can investigators reduce digital forensics backlogs in VAWG cases?**


Investigators can reduce backlogs by triaging evidence so the most relevant devices and content are reviewed first, instead of examining every device in full.[Cellebrite Genesis](https://cellebrite.com/en/products/cellebrite-genesis/) , AI built for investigations, triages large volumes of case evidence and traces every finding back to its source.
